clue.text: Dave made an alternative biblical origin story

blocks.note: anagram fodder, 10 letters

explanation.walkthrough: Dave contributes nothing but his letters — 'alternative' does the shuffling. Two biblical names make the answer hard to see in such a modern, chatty surface.

clue.text: Current measures while politician is inside

blocks.note: while = AS, the two-letter shell
the usual Member of Parliament

explanation.walkthrough: AS meaning 'while' is a workhorse container shell — two letters that swallow almost anything — and MP is one of the first abbreviations every solver learns. 'Current' here is electrical, not up to date.

clue.text: Queue said to follow these characters on the summit

blocks.note: 'queue' said aloud is the letter Q
the letters that come right after Q in the alphabet, read together, sound out the answer

explanation.walkthrough: Say 'queue' aloud and you have the letter Q, which comes straight after the characters A to P. Read the answer as 'A to P' and the alphabet joke lands.

clue.text: Champion, before successful putt, reveals secret edge

blocks.note: an ace is a champion
where a successful putt leaves the ball

explanation.walkthrough: 'Before' just sets the order: ACE, then where a holed putt ends up. The phrase itself comes from poker, not golf — the face-down card that gives you a hidden advantage.

clue.text: Cover beginnings of debate regarding act prohibiting euthanasia

blocks.note: the beginnings — first letters — of the five words

explanation.walkthrough: 'Beginnings of' points at the initial letters of the five words that follow. The sombre parliamentary surface is a decoy; the clue is a pure acrostic.

clue.text: Indirect service provider promises to pay

blocks.note: the service is a church service, so its provider is a vicar
IOUs are written promises to pay

explanation.walkthrough: 'Service provider' wants you thinking broadband; the service is in a church. Vicarious pleasure is felt indirectly, through someone else — hence the definition.

clue.text: Component of post-operative check

blocks.note: hidden inside poST-OPerative

explanation.walkthrough: 'Component of' flags a hidden word, and the hyphen is no barrier — hidden answers run straight across punctuation. 'Check' as in halt something.

clue.text: Drama created by one stealing chips

blocks.note: a specific Chekhov play from 1896 — title and definite article both count as the definition
the British seaside menace that swoops on your lunch

explanation.walkthrough: Chekhov's play — and the definite article works hard, because at the seaside the seagull really is the one stealing your chips.

clue.text: Difficult spot with picturesque route through mountains

blocks.note: an old idiom for landing in a sorry state
a mountain pass that happens to be pretty

explanation.walkthrough: 'Come to a pretty pass' is an old idiom for landing in a sorry state; a mountain pass can certainly be pretty. One phrase, two readings, no letters moved.

clue.text: History of article found in French region

blocks.note: the indefinite article
AN drops inside it

explanation.walkthrough: Provence supplies the shell and the article drops in. Provenance is the history of an object's ownership — an auction-house word, which is why 'History' alone defines it.

clue.text: Widespread idea setter repeated

blocks.note: the setter referring to himself
and again — 'repeated' is the whole of the second half, so the same two letters are written twice

explanation.walkthrough: 'Setter' pointing at the setter himself is classic crossword self-reference: ME, said twice. A meme is exactly an idea that spreads.

clue.text: One has market in chaos? I can’t answer that

blocks.note: anagram fodder, 12 letters

explanation.walkthrough: The definition is the whole exasperated phrase at the end — 'ask me another' is what you say when you can't answer. The question mark excuses the odd economics surface.

clue.text: Restrict open representation during review

indicators.note: anagram indicator: a re-presentation of the letters

blocks.note: anagram fodder, 12 letters

explanation.walkthrough: 'Representation' earns its length as the anagram signal — a re-presentation of the fodder. 'During review' captures looking back at events once they are over.

clue.text: Lama unsure about guidance it provides

blocks.note: anagram fodder, 10 letters

explanation.walkthrough: 'About' is the anagram signal, easy to dismiss as filler. The 'it' in the definition points at the answer itself: a user manual is exactly guidance it provides.

clue.text: Actors’ share that ensures kids are excluded in future

definitions.text: that ensures kids are excluded in future

blocks.note: the actors in a production
a share = a ration

explanation.walkthrough: CAST plus RATION, with a pitch-black definition: 'kids' are offspring — including baby goats, where the operation is routine — so it guarantees none in future.

clue.text: Recreation area beside slum provides very small portion of pasta

blocks.note: a spa is a recreation area
a ghetto is a slum

explanation.walkthrough: The definition is the joke: spaghetto really is the Italian singular of spaghetti — one solitary strand, the smallest possible portion of pasta.

clue.text: Kidnapped but had disagreement

blocks.note: issue = children in legal English, so kidnapping is taking someone's issue
the everyday sense: objected to or complained about something

explanation.walkthrough: 'Issue' meaning children survives mainly in legal English and in crosswords — worth memorising. The everyday sense of objecting shares exactly the same two words.

clue.text: Do some research for facelift?

blocks.note: read the one word in two halves: the first of them, 'face', is slang for MUG
and something lifted has gone up — the question mark licenses splitting the one word in two

explanation.walkthrough: To mug up is British slang for cramming a subject. The question mark licenses splitting 'facelift' in two: a mug is slang for a face, and something lifted goes up.

clue.text: Almost vomit from contents of secret chamber

blocks.note: hidden across secRET CHamber

explanation.walkthrough: 'Contents of' says look inside what follows, and the answer runs across the word break. To retch is to heave without quite succeeding — hence 'almost' vomit.

clue.text: Blocks former pupil’s heartless challenges

blocks.note: OB = old boy, the crossword's former pupil, keeping his ’s
TACKLES with its heart (the K) removed

explanation.walkthrough: OB for old boy is a standard former pupil, and his possessive S is part of the build. 'Heartless' then strips the middle letter from TACKLES.

clue.text: Limbo dancer’s record performance? It couldn’t be worse for some

definitions.text: It couldn’t be worse for some

blocks.note: a limbo record is literally the lowest anyone has ever gone

blocks.clueFragment: It couldn’t be worse for some
blocks.note: the everyday phrase for rock bottom

explanation.walkthrough: Both halves define the same phrase: a limbo champion's record really is the lowest ever achieved, and rock bottom, for some, couldn't be worse. The question mark flags the literal reading.

clue.text: Praise plasticity of latex?

blocks.note: anagram fodder, 5 letters

explanation.walkthrough: 'Plasticity of' is the anagram signal — latex is mouldable, which is why the surface reads so naturally. Five letters reshape into a word of praise.

clue.text: Bird impersonator sounds lightweight to some

blocks.note: a lightweight concern is a minor one

explanation.walkthrough: The myna is the great avian mimic, hence 'bird impersonator'. 'To some' is the setter being honest: only in non-rhotic accents does 'minor' sound quite like MYNA.

clue.text: It protects Americans caught in calamitous aftermath

blocks.note: hidden across calamitoUS AFtermath

explanation.walkthrough: 'Caught in' flags the hidden word, running across the break in calamitoUS AFtermath — and a surface about protection after calamity suits the United States Air Force nicely.

clue.text: Incompetent fellow quits squad

blocks.note: incompetent = unfit
F = fellow, as in academic titles like FRS

explanation.walkthrough: F for fellow comes from academic honours — FRS and friends. Send him away from the middle of UNFIT and the squad remains.

clue.text: I dismiss unclear vision articulated by soul pioneer

blocks.note: said aloud: ISAAC
said aloud: HAYES

explanation.walkthrough: 'Articulated' asks you to say both halves aloud: 'I sack' and 'haze'. Isaac Hayes — the voice of Shaft — is the soul pioneer being spelled out.

clue.text: Advance! It’s part of command Nelson rejected

blocks.note: hidden across commanD NELson

explanation.walkthrough: The fragment hides across 'command Nelson' and 'rejected' sends it back — a backwards reading, which suits an across entry. 'Advance' means lend, as a bank advances money.

clue.text: Spouse felt breath getting uneven

blocks.note: anagram fodder, 10 letters

explanation.walkthrough: 'Getting uneven' shakes up the fodder. 'Better half' is the affectionate term for a spouse — a warm answer hiding in a worrying surface about laboured breathing.
